correctness.rationale: A four-center covering lower bound and a parity-class coverage argument force an exhaustive 16+24 structural classification of all 40 minimum Q4 dominating sets. Four pair-orbit count arrays and six triple-orbit count arrays (which sum to 560 triples) yield the full static result; for each triple precisely one of eight traces is absent. An 8-leaf explicit adaptive tree proves depth three; pair co-occurrence counts and disjoint remainders prove the positive root branch has depth at most two, excluding depth four. Independent Python and C++17 implementations enumerate all candidates and replay all 560 triple checks and 28,409 reachable online subfamilies. The claim is strictly finite and does not extrapolate.

value.rationale: The seven-of-eight law is uniform across all 560 triples of a canonical optimum one-error covering family, establishing an exact boundary between universal pair shattering and near-universal triple traces. The strict VC=2 versus Littlestone=3 separation identifies a genuinely adaptive learning behavior not contained in the cardinality or orbit census; the conclusion is a motivated natural invariant, with a fully classified missing-pattern geometry and a complete finite proof rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
